title: Video evidence A
prompt: Watch the complete clip and record your assessment before revealing six saved classifier outputs. Compare their frame-by-frame behaviour, then decide what the results can and cannot establish.
explanation: Dataset-labelled authentic video from AIGVDBench (CVPR 2026), sourced by its authors from OpenVid-HD; exact archive member videos/QXqbhkHBRvA_0_70to196.mp4. Downloaded at pinned dataset revision bf48acaa4920990af3dd2a511ea88e63354df305; no trimming, transcoding, watermark removal or other media edit. Selected by visual inspection before running the final six-detector comparison because its high-key studio presentation can look synthetic. This is a purpose-selected teaching case, not a random sample. The two clips were independently selected and are not claimed to share a prompt or identity. The public release does not expose a verified mapping from the numeric closed-source filename to the real-video IDs. The source label is publisher documentation, not signed provenance or independent authentication. UniversalFakeDetect, Community Forensics, SPAI, AIDE and FatFormer were run as image classifiers on the same eight evenly spaced frames; GenD analysed face crops from those frames and addresses the narrower face-manipulation task. Five outputs are very low and AIDE is higher but still uncalibrated; that pattern does not authenticate the clip. None of the six analyses motion, temporal consistency, lip-sync or audio. Their outputs are uncalibrated and must not be averaged into a truth score. This deliberately difficult two-clip case study is not an accuracy benchmark. Dataset card licence declaration: CC BY 4.0; upstream rights were not independently audited.
